Only one PR was updated in the window, so here is the full list plus context:

  1. #5373 — docs: add Simplified Chinese Copilot CLI README (open). Adds zh-CN translation with EN/zh navigation links; preserves commands and config keys. Community localization effort — relevant given the IME/input issues above.

Note: no code PRs landed in the last 24h per the provided data; release notes indicate feature work is merging via the release pipeline rather than visible PRs.

5. Hot Discussions

No discussion data was provided for this window — section omitted.

6. Feature Request Trends

  • Input model configurability: user-defined submit key, correct Shift+Enter newline semantics, IME-safe behavior, and disabling built-in slash commands (#5375) so custom skills aren't shadowed by /review.
  • Model routing control: model block-lists for Fusion/Auto (#5369), 1-hour Claude cache TTL (#5220).
  • Context/token economics: model-judged pruning of junk tool results (#5362), scrollback collapsing to highlight Q/A turns (#4995).
  • Extensibility hooks: authoritative foreground-session change hook (#5279), display-only redaction hook (#5099), desktop rendering of postToolUse output (#5374).
  • Enterprise/BYOK resilience: configurable retry/backoff (#3679), BYOK providers honored in --server/--host-environment modes (#5371), OTel export in ACP mode (#5376).

7. Developer Pain Points

  • Entra/MCP OAuth is the #1 reliability gap: three related open issues (#5236, #5250, #5366) describe empty token caches, concurrent sign-in rejection, and misleading "connected" status post-expiry. Enterprise users re-authenticate constantly or silently lose tools.
  • Input handling ignores platform realities: Shift+Enter semantics and IME Enter collisions remain unfixed despite 48 👍 and nine-comment threads — a low-effort, high-visibility fix that keeps slipping.
  • Silent failures over loud ones: delayed Fusion output (#5370), lost MCP schemas (#5367), stale OAuth status (#5366), and ACP reporting a model it isn't running (#5363) all make the agent look fine while misbehaving — eroding trust more than crashes would.
  • Non-interactive/headless parity lags the TUI: BYOK configs ignored in server modes (#5371), no OTel in ACP (#5376), session/new model mismatch (#5363) — automation users get a second-class experience.
  • Cost anxiety under default settings: 5-minute Claude cache expiry and instant 429 retry exhaustion both translate directly into wasted spend and failed runs for heavy users.

Generated from github.com/github/copilot-cli data for 2026-11-07.

OpenCode — anomalyco/opencode

OpenCode Community Digest — 2026-11-06/07

1. Today's Highlights

No new releases in the past 24 hours, but the project had a heavy triage day: a large batch of previously-reproduced bugs were closed (TUI theming, MCP OAuth, composer @ handling, agent frontmatter parsing), suggesting maintainers are clearing the deck ahead of the next release. The most active discussion remains Agent Plugins spec support (#40993, 21 👍), while the Code Mode VM work from jlongster landed in a "dev-by-default" PR. Community sentiment is mixed: strong enthusiasm for extensibility (plugins, subagent limits), with recurring frustration around model quality, desktop/Windows stability, and the free-model experience.

2. Releases

No new releases in the last 24 hours.

3. Hot Issues

  1. #40993 — Support the Agent Plugins standard (OPEN, 17 comments, 21 👍) Requests support for agent-plugins.org, the vendor-neutral packaging spec bundling Agent Skills + MCP servers. Highest-engagement open issue; signals users want portable plugin ecosystems rather than OpenCode-specific config.

  2. #27110 — Setting to limit max parallel subagents (OPEN, 14 comments, 42 👍) The most-liked issue in this window. Local-model users hit memory/context ceilings when subagents fan out uncontrollably. A simple config cap would unlock local-model workflows — clear low-effort/high-value request.

  3. #48826 — V2 subagent marks completed early with pending background work (OPEN, reproduced, 13 comments) Subagents with background: true task/shell work report completed prematurely; results are never collected by the parent. This is a correctness bug in the V2 orchestration core — probably the most impactful open bug in the list.

  4. #28030 — Delete projects in OpenCode Desktop (CLOSED, 11 comments, 15 👍) Basic project lifecycle management finally addressed in Desktop. Long-overdue UX gap; closure without a linked PR in this window merits watching for the follow-up.

  5. #7487 — exec variable substitution (OPEN, 9 comments) Users want config-style variable substitution in exec commands (e.g., for ripgrep args). Small feature, long tail — open since January, indicating configurability friction accumulates over time.

  6. #61511 — Crouton Alpha stalls mid-turn (CLOSED, 7 comments) Agent stops after a few tool calls and requires nudging. Closed recently; may reflect a hotfix or model-side change. Watch for regression reports.

  7. #61481 — Models list empty on Windows Desktop (2.2.4/2.2.5) (CLOSED, 6 comments) Critical Windows usability bug: models toggled on but "No models found" in chat. Closure suggests a fix shipped in the next desktop build; Windows reliability is a recurring theme.

  8. #40096 — Collapsible tool output in TUI (OPEN, 5 comments) Tool output renders fully expanded, drowning long sessions in noise. A /collapse toggle is exactly the kind of TUI ergonomics request that repeatedly resurfaces (see PR #62437 below).

  9. #57844 — Stray CJK glyphs in Russian answers with GLM (OPEN, 4 comments) Multilingual corruption from glm-5.3-flash-free; sibling issue #62411 (Polish) was closed same-day. Suggests a model-serving/config issue on the built-in opencode-go provider rather than user error.

  10. #62432 — Disable persisting "Allow always" approvals (CLOSED, 3 comments) "Allow always" persistently overrides ask rules in opencode.json with no opt-out. A notable security/trust gap: one click silently weakens configured permissions. Closed quickly — verify whether it was fixed or triaged away.

4. Key PR Progress

  1. #62446 — docs(console): deprecate Pulse Alpha Free Free period ended; moved to Deprecated models. Routine but user-visible for free-tier users.

  2. #62444 — feat(core): Code Mode VM default-on in dev via flag registry Integrates codemode_vm into the standard ConfigFlag.registry; removes hand-rolled vmEnabled. Indicates Code Mode is progressing toward default enablement.

  3. #62413 — feat(codemode): expose suspendable program API Public API for VM suspend/resume, snapshots, and outcomes. Important for plugin authors building long-running tools; complements #62444.

  4. #58846 — fix(core): repair V1 global sessions left by completed imports Follow-up to #56322 for users who already upgraded past the migration window. Data-integrity fix for long-time users.

  5. #62249 — fix(core): keep grep results when a match isn't UTF-8 Grep currently fails outright on Latin-1/GBK files. Small robustness fix with real impact for non-ASCII codebases.

  6. #62437 — feat(tui): collapse tool details behind a clickable header Revives the stale-bot-closed #42552 in response to #40096. Adds session.tool_details (show/collapse). Strong signal maintainers are listening to long-standing TUI ergonomics feedback.

  7. #62250 — fix(core): keep agents whose description starts with a bracketed tag Fixes silent AgentNotFoundError from YAML parsing [Tag] ... as a flow sequence. The "silently dropped with no warning" aspect is the real complaint.

  8. #62245 — fix(tui): return to MCP list after OAuth sign-in Multiple MCP OAuth servers no longer require reopening the dialog each time. Quality-of-life for MCP-heavy users.

  9. #62248 — fix(tui): prefer terminal light/dark mode over cached palette Fixes dark TUI on light terminals when a stale palette is cached. Part of the batch of TUI reliability fixes.

  10. #62201 — fix(app): show re-imported sessions after deletion Deleted-then-reimported sessions stayed hidden until restart. Bug fix plus a signal that session lifecycle consistency matters for workspace UX.

5. Hot Discussions

No standalone Discussion data was provided; issue-level discussion is covered in Hot Issues.

6. Feature Request Trends

  • Agent/platform extensibility: Agent Plugins standard (#40993), plugin API for session.synthetic wake-if-idle (#62324), ACP session steering (#62208), exec variable substitution (#7487). The plugin/API surface is the clearest growth direction.
  • Subagent orchestration controls: parallel-subagent caps (#27110), plus correctness bugs in background subagent completion (#48826) and steering (#53615).
  • TUI/Desktop ergonomics: collapsible tool output (#40096), project deletion (#28030), model favorites toggle (#50969), theme-mode handling (#52457).
  • Permission/trust controls: opt-out of persisted "Allow always" (#62432), explicit ask enforcement.

7. Developer Pain Points

  • Local model constraints: parallel context limits make fan-out subagent patterns unusable without a cap (#27110) — highest 👍 count in the dataset.
  • Windows/Desktop instability: empty models list (#61481), ResizeObserver error storms with 33–37 MB dumps (#62206), double-quoted prompt args (#62202). Windows remains the weakest platform.
  • Free/model-quality issues: GLM multilingual corruption (#57844, #62411), hosted web_search silently dropped for gpt-6-luna (#61614), ECONNRESET on free models (#62179) — free-tier reliability is eroding trust.
  • Silent failures: dropped agents on bracketed YAML descriptions (#54200), ignored V2 permissions when name is present (#62415), npm registry ignore behind corporate mirrors (#62403). Users repeatedly ask for warnings/errors instead of silent degradation.
  • Long-standing small gaps: exec variable substitution open since January (#7487); tool-output noise requests years in the making — small papercuts that compound over time.
Pi — earendil-works/pi

Pi Community Digest — 2026-11-07

1. Today's Highlights

A high-velocity maintenance day: no releases, but 50 issues and 21 PRs updated in 24h, with most fixes landing via the robopipi[bot]/petrroll pairing. The dominant themes were file-encoding and line-ending integrity in the edit tool (mixed CRLF/LF and non-UTF-8 files silently corrupted), fullscreen TUI rendering on Orca/WezTerm-style terminals, and a cluster of provider-adapter robustness fixes (openai-completions empty tools: [], duplicate tool-call stream indexes, retry patterns for truncated streams). A prio:p0 regression — the new StringEnum in pi-ai 1.5.0 breaking compile-time tool parameter typing — was filed and is the most consequential open item for extension authors.

2. Releases

None in the last 24h.

3. Hot Issues

  1. #7730 — [OPEN] High CPU usage on macOS with long sessions (30 comments, 👍12) — The most-discussed issue in the repo. CPU swings 50–110% with 600–800MB memory, anecdotally correlated with context/session length. Long-standing (since Aug) and still unresolved: a real reliability concern for users running sustained agent sessions. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/7730

  2. #1188 — [CLOSED] Better screen-reader compatibility (14 comments) — The "working" spinner re-renders every 80ms, flooding screen readers with updates. Closed after a long thread; a good example of accessibility feedback being driven to resolution. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/1188

  3. #10605 — [OPEN] ChatGPT/OpenAI OAuth 403 "not eligible for subscription sharing" (13 comments, 👍1) — Blocks OpenAI Plus subscribers from authenticating. Auth-path failures of this kind tend to escalate quickly because they completely block a provider. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10605

  4. #8810 — [OPEN] Extension-registered providers intermittently ignored for defaultProvider/defaultModel (10 comments, 👍5) — Fresh sessions sometimes fall back to another provider's default when the configured one is registered via pi.registerProvider. Deterministic-looking misconfiguration that isn't; high impact for multi-provider setups. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/8810

  5. #11869 — [OPEN] prio:p0: new StringEnum in 1.5.0 breaks compile-time typing (2 comments, 👍2) — StringEnum no longer derives from typebox, so TParam inference in registerTool collapses to unknown. A self-inflicted 1.5.0 regression that will bite every extension author using enum tool params. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11869

  6. #11876 — [CLOSED] edit/read tools bypassed by sed in shell (3 comments) — Observed with claude-opus-5.5/sonnet-5.5 on Windows: the model shells out to sed instead of using the structured tools, silently rewriting line endings. Ties directly into the line-ending bug cluster. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11876

  7. #11858 — [CLOSED] codemode script repeated an identical tool call 24,018 times (3 comments) — ~680 calls/s, each reading a 28KB file, stopped only by wall-clock abort. No per-script repetition guard exists; a sandbox-safety gap worth tracking even though closed as no-action. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11858

  8. #10585 — [OPEN] bash temp-file stream errors crash the whole process (ENOSPC/EACCES) (4 comments) — On 1.0.4, a full /tmp produced an uncaught exception that killed the run and lost the in-flight session log. Resource-exhaustion resilience for the bash tool. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10585

  9. #11317 — [OPEN] SDK: customize identity preamble without replacing default prompt sections (4 comments) — Request to allow systemPromptOptions.sections.preamble overrides while keeping Pi's tools/rules/docs. A recurring SDK-customization request (see also #11863). https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11317

  10. #11880 — [CLOSED] Session files contain role: "system" with empty content, breaking transcript readers (2 comments) — Every session's fourth line is a system message that third-party viewers choke on. Closed no-action, but it's a real interop footgun for anyone parsing session files. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11880

4. Key PR Progress

  1. #11751 — [CLOSED] edit preserves line endings of untouched lines — Fixes #8544: the tool rewrote every line to the style of the first newline, silently mutating mixed CRLF/LF files. Also avoids post-write diff OOM on large files. Non-UTF-8/UTF-16 handling split into a follow-up. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11751

  2. #11894 — [OPEN] edit refuses non-valid-UTF-8 files — Follow-up to #11751: GBK/Windows-1252/UTF-16 files currently have undecodable bytes replaced with U+FFFD while reporting success. The proposed behavior is to fail loudly instead of corrupting. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11894

  3. #11895 — [CLOSED] grep globs matched relative to path, not cwd — Fixes #11807: { path: "repo", glob: "migrations/main/*.js" } returned "No matches found" because ripgrep rooted --glob at the process cwd. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11895

  4. #11896 — [CLOSED] Await image resize worker termination — Fixes #10695: void worker.terminate() in finally allowed overlapping teardown/startup, aborting Pi on macOS arm64 / Node 24. Serial image reads were the reproducer. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11896

  5. #11891 — [CLOSED] Omit empty tools: [] for openai-completions — Fixes #11843: requests without tools but with tool history in the transcript sent "tools": [], which vLLM 0.20+ (and LiteLLM in front of it) rejects with a 400. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11891

  6. #11882 — [CLOSED] Split tool-call blocks when stream index and tool-call id disagree — Fixes #11881: providers reusing the same tool_calls[].index for distinct ids caused two argument streams to be concatenated into one malformed tool call. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11882

  7. #11890 — [CLOSED] Draw fullscreen Kitty images after the rows they cover — Fixes #11835: Orca and WezTerm implement Kitty graphics as cell tiles, so TuiAltScreen's draw order left only the first row visible. Terminal-specific TUI correctness. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11890

  8. #11885 — [CLOSED] Retry streams cut short after the reply had begun — Added an isRetryableAssistantError() pattern for Anthropic streams dropped mid-reply through the Magpie gateway; previously not retried. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11885

  9. #11873 — [CLOSED] Keep apostrophes in prompt template arguments — Fixes #11861: parseCommandArgs treated every ' as opening a quote, turning why doesn't the user's cache work into why doesnt the users cache work. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11873

  10. #11888 — [CLOSED] Record live thinking level on the branch before each prompt — Fixes #11451: /tree rewinds could leave the latest thinking_level_change on an abandoned branch, so resume restored a stale level. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11888

5. Hot Discussions

Show and tell

  • #11860 — CaseClip: save a Pi mistake as a reviewable case card 👍1 — /case save <what went wrong> captures the latest request, tool result, and user correction together. Motivated by a demo where Pi called a retired API, got a 404, and still claimed success. Complements the crash/abort observability issues above. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/discussions/11860

Q&A / Ideas

  • #11870 — Keeping skills organized across Pi, Claude Code, and OpenCode 👍1 — Duplicate skill directories drifting apart across agents; author built AgentKeeper (macOS app + CLI) to catalog them. Points at a cross-agent skill/packaging ecosystem gap. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/discussions/11870

6. Feature Request Trends

  • SDK prompt customization: composable systemPromptOptions (preamble/identity without replacing defaults, #11317) plus guidance on long-running multimodal context management (#11863).
  • Provider/catalog coverage: recurring requests to add models to bundled catalogs (kimi-coding k3.1-pro, Z.AI glm-5.3-flashx, QwenCloud deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 — #11883, #11884, #11877).
  • Session/transcript interoperability: stable, reader-friendly session files (#11880) and terminal-title reporting via OSC 7501 (#11670) for agent dashboards.
  • Resource governance: per-conversation compaction policy in pi-durable (#11771), and sandbox guards against runaway tool-call loops (#11858).
  • Cross-agent skill management: deduplication of skills across Pi/Claude Code/OpenCode (#11870).

7. Developer Pain Points

  • Silent file corruption in edit: mixed line endings (#8544, #11876) and non-UTF-8 files (#11894) were mutated while the tool reported success. This was clearly the highest-priority correctness fix of the day.
  • Provider-adapter edge cases: empty tools: [] vs. vLLM/LiteLLM (#11843), duplicate stream indexes from non-conforming OpenAI-compatible providers (#11881), unclassified mid-stream drops (#11885), and the OpenAI OAuth 403 (#10605). Non-first-party gateways remain a friction source.
  • Auth/token lifecycle: Copilot 401/403-before-expiry refresh (#10238) and the OAuth subscription-sharing error point at a need for more defensive token refresh.
  • Resource exhaustion kills the process: ENOSPC/EACCES on bash temp files (#10585), image-worker teardown races (#10695), and leaked provider sessions from Harness.close() (#11676) all terminate or hang work rather than degrading gracefully.
  • Typing regressions in the extension API: the StringEnum/typebox decoupling in 1.5.0 (#11869) is a p0 DX issue for anyone writing typed tools.
  • Platform-specific gaps: Windows SIGHUP/process-tree cleanup (#11889, #11854), Windows path/prompt quoting (#11873, #11861, #11874), and macOS session CPU (#7730) suggest platform testing coverage is thinner than the core path.
Qwen Code — QwenLM/qwen-code

Qwen Code Community Digest — 2026-11-07

1. Today's Highlights

Release v0.26.9 lands with skill installation/activation improvements (ZIP uploads, daemon APIs, TypeScript SDK support, bulk activation, recovery protections). CI stability remains the dominant theme: the bot-filed #14724 "Managed Agent gate" issue has ballooned to 217 comments and is still open. Meanwhile, two P1 bugs drew attention — a workflow-agent approval deadlock in the interactive TUI (#16425, with fix PR #16432 already up) and a session-corruption report around auto-compaction (#16418).

2. Releases

v0.26.9 — no full changelog details were provided beyond the highlights block.

  • Skill installation and activation: Skill ZIP uploads, daemon APIs, TypeScript SDK support, bulk activation, and recovery protections make installing and managing skills easier.
  • Breaking changes: None known.

→ https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/releases

3. Hot Issues

  1. #14724 — Main CI failed: Managed Agent gate (217 comments, OPEN) — The longest-running CI failure thread; a signal that the managed-agent gate is chronically flaky and consuming maintainer bandwidth. → https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/issues/14724

  2. #13113 — P1: "Transcript snapshot is too large to index" (256 MiB hardcoded limit) — file_history_snapshot grows quadratically, making long sessions permanently unopenable. A serious data-durability concern for heavy users. → https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/issues/13113

  3. #15597 — P1: Headless -p auto-memory can never save — The implicit edit/write deny overrides memory agents' scoped allow, so auto-memory silently no-ops while still costing tokens. High-impact for automation users. → https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/issues/15597

  4. #16425 — P1: Workflow agent approval never renders, run hangs indefinitely — Approvals fire but no UI surfaces them, deadlocking background workflow agents (reproduced on 0.26.8). Fix PR #16432 is already open. → https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/issues/16425

  5. #16418 — P1: Auto-compaction turns review-only skill into unauthorized implementation — Repeated compaction appears to erode skill scoping, causing the agent to implement code it was only authorized to review. Safety-relevant. → https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/issues/16418

  6. #15412 — P2: Long project paths break chat recording and session list — Full absolute paths flattened into a single filesystem component exceed macOS limits, breaking sessions for deeply nested projects. → https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/issues/15412

  7. #15310 — P3: Tell the model which shell it uses (Windows) — On Windows the model assumes bash and emits POSIX commands via cmd.exe, burning a full turn per failure. Simple, high-leverage fix. → https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/issues/15310

  8. #15495 — P2: Image payload eviction has no off switch — Inline images are silently rewritten out of history at an undocumented threshold of 20; users want configurability. (Addressed by PR #16438.) → https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/issues/15495

  9. #16457 — P2: MCP OAuth flows share fixed callback port 7777 — Overlapping OAuth flows invalidate each other's state, blocking multi-MCP-server auth setups. → https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/issues/16457

  10. #15800 — P2: Background shell status stuck "running" after abrupt session end — Status files never reconcile with finished processes, misleading users about live background jobs. → https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/issues/15800

4. Key PR Progress

  1. #16432 — fix(cli): surface workflow agent approvals in the interactive TUI — Directly fixes P1 #16425 by requiring a real responder before parking an approval. The most time-sensitive fix in flight. → https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16432

  2. #16438 — fix(config): declare model.chatCompression knobs; allow disabling image eviction — Adds 0 = never evict for image payloads, closing #15495 and exposing hidden settings. → https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16438

  3. #16075 — fix(permissions): match amend invocations instead of raw text — Reworks the AUTO-mode amend guard to parse shell invocations (compound splitting, heredoc stripping, wrapper unwrapping) rather than regex raw text. Security hardening. → https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16075

  4. #16454 — fix(telemetry): report OpenAI cache_write_tokens as cache creation — Restores cache-write accounting in GenAI telemetry for both streaming and non-streaming paths (fixes #15414). → https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16454

  5. #15936 — fix(core): reduce or refuse compression requests that can't fit their window — Guarantees ≥4,096 output tokens (or 25%) for summaries and retries once on context-length rejection. Targets long-session reliability. → https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15936

  6. #16491 — feat(core): name the active shell in startup context — Tells the model its actual shell (e.g., cmd.exe on Windows), fixing the class of failures in #15310. → https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16491

  7. #16475 — feat(managed-agent): persisted session diagnostics — Adds Public/WebShell API pairs plus a dialog with Context, Model statistics, Resources, and Child agents tabs. → https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16475

  8. #16185 — fix(core): name the model and setting in media refusals — Improves error text so the model (and user) knows why an image/audio/video was rejected and which setting caused it. → https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16185

  9. #15562 — feat(desktop): persist Web Shell catalogs across restarts — Saves daemon connections and workspace-host catalogs in the desktop shell via an allowlisted IPC surface. → https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15562

  10. #15473 — fix(desktop): stop bundled runtime before installing an update — Windows in-app updates now shut down the daemon first (kill-on-close job object), avoiding locked Node binaries. → https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15473

5. Hot Discussions

No Discussion data was provided in this dataset; this section is omitted.

6. Feature Request Trends

  • Configurability of hidden behaviors: off-switches and declared settings for image eviction (#15495), compression, and session limits (#13113).
  • Better platform awareness: shell detection on Windows (#15310), long-path handling (#15412).
  • Observability & telemetry: OpenRouter routing provider/generation ID as span attributes (#14629); persisted session diagnostics (#16475).
  • Memory & extensibility: proposals for pluggable long-term memory (#16429 bzmem), MCP OAuth robustness (#16457).
  • UI/UX: OSC 7501 program-status reporting (#13870), inline branch chat for Web Shell (#16474).
  • Multi-agent reliability: approval surfacing and background-view UX (#16425, #16444).

7. Developer Pain Points

  • CI flakiness dominates maintainer attention — bot-filed main-CI failures (#14724, #15712, #16377, #16191) with enormous comment threads crowd out feature work.
  • Long-running sessions are fragile — quadratic snapshot growth (#13113), auto-compaction side effects (#16418), and stuck background-shell status (#15800) all degrade long sessions.
  • Silent no-ops cost tokens — headless auto-memory (#15597) and image eviction (#15495) do things users can't see or control.
  • Auth/multi-server friction — MCP OAuth port collisions (#16457) block multi-server setups.
  • Windows parity gaps — shell assumptions (#15310) and update-time runtime locking (#15473).
  • Cross-platform path handling — absolute-path flattening breaks macOS projects (#15412).

OpenClaw 生态日报 2026-11-07

Issues: 377 | PRs: 500 | 覆盖项目: 5 个 | 生成时间: 2026-11-06 23:16 UTC

  • OpenClaw
  • Hermes Agent
  • IronClaw

OpenClaw 项目深度报告

OpenClaw 项目摘要 — 2026-11-07

1. 今日概览

OpenClaw 仍处于高速推进但受稳定性制约的阶段：过去 24 小时内有 377 个 issue 和 500 个 PR 被更新，其中 217 个未关闭/活跃 issue、361 个未关闭 PR，而已合并/关闭 PR 为 139 个——这一合并与未关闭之比表明，瓶颈在于评审能力，而非贡献者供给。今日没有新版本发布，说明项目正处于两个发布列车之间（当前稳定线为 2026.10.10，2026.11.5-beta.1 处于预发布状态）。今日活动的主导主题是回归与生命周期/资源管理缺陷——网关事件循环阻塞、SQLite worker OOM、MCP 子进程泄漏、WAL checkpoint 饥饿以及提示缓存失效——其中多项为 P0/P1 并被标记为发布阻塞项。社区参与度是务实型的而非狂热型：困难 bug 的评论数很高（某个 P0 有 80 条评论），但整体反应数接近零，同时存在大量未解决的旧报告“陈旧”积压。

2. 发布

过去 24 小时无新版本发布。供跟踪版本的读者参考的背景信息：

  • 各 issue 中引用的当前稳定版：2026.10.10
  • 被提及仅在预发布中修复的问题：2026.11.5-beta.1（例如 #141474、#193962）
  • 多个未关闭的回归被归因于特定已发布版本（2026.9.5、2026.9.6、2026.9.8、2026.10.5、2026.10.10）

4. 社区热点话题

按评论活动排序：

  2. #164294 — 39 条评论 — SQLite WAL 自动 checkpoint 永不完成，被一个进程内读取器钉住（17,091 个日志帧 vs 866 个已 checkpoint）。典型的读取器饥饿病理。
  3. #177656 — P1，29 条评论 — 原生宿主 exec 在 2026.10.5 上返回共享状态“完整性准入”错误（≥28 次失败）。

底层需求： 社区高度关注网关作为长期运行守护进程的运维可靠性——资源遏制（插件、MCP 子进程、SQLite 读取器）和干净的生命周期命令。记忆系统行为（dreaming/提升/保留）是第二集群，表明记忆是用户在生产中重点压力测试的招牌差异化功能。

7. 用户反馈摘要

真实用户表达的痛点：

  • 升级可靠性是头号挫败。 多份报告描述升级在激活后失败（#178291）、在迁移上阻塞（#185656），甚至无法触达自身修复（#193962）。生产安装上的用户实际上被钉住。
  • 资源泄漏侵蚀对长期运行网关的信任。 评论者自行量化损害：每个 stdio MCP 子进程约 144–145 MB（#164690）、claude-cli 下重复 MCP spawn（#166017、#164690）、上限 256 的 broker 耗尽（#166017）。这是一个成熟的生产操作者受众。
  • 记忆系统行为令人困惑且有损。 用户报告 memory promote 在一个工作区返回零候选，而兄弟工作区提升 50–90%（#164923），以及夜间 dreaming 永不提升（#150635）——旗舰“dreaming”功能对部分用户未交付可见价值。
  • 静默失败和不透明错误反复成为主题：Telegram 回调被丢弃（#126950）、跨 16 个调用点的通用“changed while starting work”无原因码（#127195）、无标签的 Code Mode 内部错误（#167609），以及无日志原因的撤销（#166964）。用户在做产品本应做的诊断工作。
  • 成本焦虑是切实的：用户手工测量缓存写入 token（#143017）并恳求按模型使用日志（#13219）。
  • 移动端/UI 摩擦（手机小输入框 #139909、聊天重载回溯 PR #193217、重复渲染 #123792）是稳定的次要流。

满意度信号： 困难 bug 的评论数很高而反应数接近零——用户投入且勤勉，但并非喝彩。人们显然在严肃的生产配置中运行 OpenClaw（Kubernetes、15 个 agent 的多 agent 组织、Docker 沙箱），这既是对项目能力的赞美，也是其稳定性债务的来源。

横向生态对比

跨项目对比报告 — 个人 AI 助手 / Agent 开源生态

快照日期：2026-11-07 | 项目：OpenClaw、Hermes Agent、IronClaw、QwenPaw、ZeroClaw

1. 生态概览

Agent 框架生态正处于功能已交付、加固尚未完成的阶段：四个活跃项目都已发布其标志性能力（多 Agent 编排、记忆/梦境、插件、渠道网关），如今正在偿还由此产生的稳定性债务。活动以回归和生命周期 Bug 为主，而非新功能；安全/权限模型正成为新的战场（ZeroClaw），而长期运行网关的运维可靠性则是普遍痛点。用户群体已成熟为生产环境运维者——他们运行 Kubernetes、多 Agent 组织和加固的 Docker 部署，其反馈是量化的、诊断性的，而非愿景式的。生态健康度呈两极分化：各项目的贡献者供给都很充足，但维护者的评审能力才是真正的约束，体现为远低于 1.0 的合并/开启比，以及积压数月、因决策受阻的 PR。本窗口期内没有任何项目发布稳定版本，表明整个生态集体处于发布列车之间的间隙。

3. OpenClaw 的定位

相对同行的优势：

  • 社区规模： 24h 内 377 个 Issue + 500 个 PR 有更新，约为 Hermes 或 QwenPaw 活动量的 7–10 倍，约 15 倍于 ZeroClaw。OpenClaw 拥有最深厚的贡献者池和最成熟的生产运维者（K8s 部署、15 Agent 组织、Docker 沙箱）。
  • 最广的覆盖面： 记忆/梦境系统、MCP 集成、插件 SDK、多渠道（Telegram、msteams、iOS）、云 worker、Code Mode 以及 Control UI——无同行能匹敌这一广度。
  • 参考实现地位： 被定位为"核心参考"实现；同行隐含地以其为基准。

技术路线差异：

  • OpenClaw 以长期运行的 Gateway 守护进程为架构中心——这既是其力量来源（持久会话、定时任务、渠道汇聚），也是其稳定性债务来源（事件循环阻塞、SQLite worker OOM、MCP 子进程泄漏）。QwenPaw 等同行更偏向请求/会话导向，运行时足迹更轻。
  • 更重地依赖 SQLite + worker 进程和提示缓存来控制成本——二者当前都处于病态（缓存失效 #182891、worker OOM #191847），这是 Hermes/ZeroClaw 在同规模下不具备的成本与可靠性风险敞口。
  • 成熟的插件 SDK + 托管目录（附有开放请求 #164620，要求为气隙环境禁用目录源）——这是同行仍在建设中的治理面。

社区规模对比： OpenClaw 单个硬 Bug 的评论活动（#160959 上有 80 条评论）超过 QwenPaw 或 ZeroClaw 的全天互动总量。Hermes 最热帖子（#97681，40 条评论）只有 OpenClaw 最热帖子的一半。OpenClaw 是生态的引力中心；风险在于其评审能力未能随社区同步扩展。

升级/更新可靠性 更新路径探测死锁（#193962）、迁移阻塞（#185656） Windows 更新器版本陈旧（#143656）、陈旧快照恢复（#147938） 2.2/2.3/2.4 之间的版本偏斜（#8580） — OpenClaw/Hermes/QwenPaw 显著： 更新器是信任链中最薄弱的一环

综合： 生态已收敛到四个共同痛点簇——持久会话状态、可强制执行的权限、可诊断的失败、生命周期资源卫生。这些是架构性的，而非一次性的，代表着下一代框架工作。

5. 差异化分析

维度 OpenClaw Hermes Agent QwenPaw ZeroClaw
功能焦点 最广的平台：记忆/梦境、MCP、插件、多渠道、云 worker 跨网关多 Agent 协作（#97681）、桌面/群聊、插件目录 渠道插件（Matrix/IM）、记忆检索/重排、Creator UI 安全优先：主体/权限模型、SOP、cron 审批、Rust/WASM UI
目标用户 大规模生产运维者（K8s、多 Agent 组织） 多表面团队（桌面 + Webapp/PWA + 移动端）、Bot 运维者 企业 IM 用户（飞书/钉钉/Matrix）、中文 Windows 用户、离线/气隙环境 安全意识强的部署、代理/网关运维者
技术架构 长期运行 Gateway 守护进程；SQLite + worker；重提示缓存；插件 SDK Gateway + 桌面/Webapp 表面；会话 DB 后端接缝正走向 PostgreSQL（#150332） 更轻的请求/会话运行时；渠道插件模型；动态 MCP 基于 Rust；事件溯源会话历史方向（#10526）；严格权限执行；Windows/Unix
发布理念 Beta 列车与稳定版并行；快速打补丁 快速扩展次要表面（v0.22→v0.23），回归负载高 控制台 beta 线 + 后端元数据；接近 1:1 的分诊 安全闸门式切割（v0.9.0）被大型 XL PR 阻塞
生态模型 托管插件目录（已有退出请求） 社区插件目录（大量 PR） 插件包 + Creator 插件注册源（#12216）、多模型配置（#9809）

总结： OpenClaw 是平台型打法（广度 + 规模），Hermes 是协作/表面型打法（多网关、多表面），QwenPaw 是集成/本地化型打法（渠道、Windows、离线），ZeroClaw 是安全/架构型打法（Rust、权限、事件溯源）。它们更多是互补而非直接竞争——但都在争夺同一个"个人 Agent 运行时"的位置。

成熟度信号：

  • 成熟度最高： OpenClaw（规模、运维者最广，但评审紧张）和 QwenPaw（吞吐平衡）。

  • 未知： IronClaw（信号不足）。

7. 趋势信号 — 对 AI Agent 开发者的价值

从跨项目社区反馈中提炼，按战略重要性排序：

  1. 运行时可靠性就是新功能。 每个项目的头号 Bug 都是守护进程级的：事件循环阻塞、SQLite worker OOM、子进程泄漏、空闲会话泄漏、启动竞态。开发者应将生命周期资源管理视为一等设计关注点，而非事后补丁。预计框架级方案（监督器、有界 worker、背压）将成为赢家的差异化因素。

  2. 权限与审批治理是下一个竞争面。 ZeroClaw 的 S0 所有权绕过、Hermes 的审批闸门绕过和桌面审批请求、OpenClaw 的 exec 审批缺口都指向同一方向：用户希望对 Agent 的行为和记忆/技能写入拥有可见、可强制执行、基于 diff 的管控。在 UI（而非仅 CLI）中呈现审批、并在写入路径强制执行的产品将赢得信任。

  3. 会话状态正被重构为持久且可重放。 OpenClaw（SQLite worker/WAL）、Hermes（state.db + PostgreSQL 接缝 #150332）、ZeroClaw（事件溯源历史 #10526、持久对等回合 #9597）和 QwenPaw（聊天状态缓存）都在向事件溯源或仅追加、跨表面会话存储收敛。这是本窗口期最大的单一架构趋势。

  4. 成本可见性与缓存正确性是可变现的痛点。 OpenClaw 用户手动测量出 2130 万缓存写入 token（#143017），并恳求按模型用量日志（#13219）；ZeroClaw 修复了提示缓存顺序 Bug（#12176）。提示缓存纪律与用量计量现在已是任何生产框架的入场门槛。

  5. 静默失败是信任的头号杀手。 在所有项目中，被提及最多的挫败不是崩溃，而是静默丢弃、误报和无原因错误（OpenClaw #127195，Hermes #148831/#130072，QwenPaw #8276/#8234，ZeroClaw #9779/#12155）。带可操作原因码的快速失败校验是廉价、高影响的差异化因素。

  6. 升级路径是最薄弱的一环。 更新路径死锁（OpenClaw #193962）、迁移阻塞（#185656）、陈旧快照恢复（Hermes #147938）、版本偏斜（QwenPaw 2.2/2.3/2.4）。可靠、可回滚、可自校验的更新器是被忽视的需求——对工具供应商而言是一个可行的投资领域。

  7. 多表面与跨机器协作是需求前沿。 Hermes 的 #97681（40 条评论，待决策）以及桌面/群聊回归簇；OpenClaw 的多 Agent 运维者请求（#166678 从选择器隐藏、#103067 子 Agent 生命周期）。用户正从单 Agent 转向协调的多 Agent、多表面部署，速度快于框架的会话/权限模型所能支撑的程度。

  8. 本地化与离线/气隙运行是真实市场。 QwenPaw 的离线安装（#1453）、Windows/GBK 问题（#8234、#8585），以及 OpenClaw 的禁用托管目录请求（#164620）表明来自受监管、气隙和非英语生产环境的需求——这是一个被忽视的细分市场。

对开发者的底线： 生态的重心已从Agent 能做什么转向能否被信任持续做下去——持久地、安全地、可见地、可负担地。解决会话持久性、权限执行、可诊断性和更新可靠性的框架将定义下一个发布周期；功能广度已被商品化。

本报告依据 2026-11-07 的 OpenClaw、Hermes Agent、IronClaw、QwenPaw 和 ZeroClaw 摘要汇编。活动计数为所报告的 24 小时快照；健康评分为分析师综合判断。

  • #147938（P0，Windows 数据完整性）— 鉴于潜在数据丢失，需维护者立即接手。

建议： 优先分诊 P0 Windows state.db 问题（#147938）和安全绕过（#150329），解除 #102928 的阻塞，并清理 needs-decision 积压（#97681、#84189、#86105、#85342），这是合并 PR 吞吐量和社区情绪的主要拖累。

摘要基于 2026-11-07 的 GitHub 活动生成。链接指向 NousResearch/hermes-agent 仓库。

IronClaw — nearai/ironclaw

过去24小时无活动。

QwenPaw — agentscope-ai/QwenPaw

QwenPaw 项目摘要 — 2026-11-07

1. 今日概览

QwenPaw 展现出高维护活跃度：过去 24 小时内有 22 个 issue 和 38 个 PR 被处理，其中 20 个 PR 已合并/关闭，18 个仍处于打开状态——吞吐量与积压量接近 1:1。活动以稳定性与正确性修复为主，而非新功能开发：内存检索、provider 配置校验、通道插件（Matrix）以及 Windows 特有的路径处理。本次没有发布新版本，因此项目仍停留在 2.3.0b2 控制台版本线，而 2.4 后端包已在现场流通。社区互动按单项来看较为温和（大多为 1–4 条评论，零反应），表明分流覆盖面广但深度较浅。整体项目健康度：强劲——维护者的关闭速度与用户的提交速度相当，多个长期遗留 issue（可追溯至 2026 年 3 月）终于得到解决。

2. 发布

无。 过去 24 小时内没有新发布。注意：现场仍分散在 2.2.2、2.3.0b2（控制台）和 2.4 后端元数据之间，若干缺陷报告正源于此版本错配（例如 #8580 报告 UI v2.3.0b2 搭配后端 2.4 和 reme_ai 0.4.2.0）。

3. 项目进展

以下已关闭/已合并事项代表了今日的实质性推进：

已落地的修复（已关闭的 PR / issue）：

  • Provider 配置校验 — #8550（修复 #8549）：超出范围的 thinking_budget / max_input_length 现在会在写入路径被拒绝，而不再静默持久化并在重启后破坏 provider 发现。
  • Matrix 通道恢复 — #8411（修复 #8365）：在服务端设备丢失后，缓存会话得到恢复，缺失的 E2EE 设备密钥被重新上传。
  • 第三方 agent 定时任务 — #8535（修复 #8533）：Codex/Qoder cron 任务不再因 Third-party agent requests require text or attachments 而失败。
  • 动态 MCP 持久化 — #373（首次贡献者，自 3 月起打开）：动态加载的 MCP 工具现在可跨会话轮次持久化。
  • 控制台聊天切换状态 — #8600：/clear 的聊天在重新打开后保持为空（修复 #8596）。
  • 测试稳定性 — #8604、#7858：Windows shell 取消挂起和未 await 协程警告已解决。

仍在审查中（高价值）：

  • #8234 — read/edit/grep 中的 GBK/CP936 解码（修复中文 Windows 上的静默字节丢失）。
  • #8457 — 自动记忆召回以参考上下文形式注入，而非合成 assistant 轨迹。
  • #8472 — 带多查询精度历史的 reranker 模型中心。

4. 社区热点话题

互动分散；评论最多的条目（各 4 条评论）集中在内存标记和聊天状态行为上。

条目 评论数 链接 潜在需求
#8580 内存标签索引返回 503 4 链接 启用 auto_memory_generate_tags 的用户期望标签可读，而不仅仅是生成。索引重建的可靠性是内存子系统的信任问题。
#8596 /clear 消息重新出现 4 链接 聊天状态缓存正确性——用户依赖 /clear 语义进行隐私/重置工作流。
#1453 离线安装无法连接本地 Qwen 4 链接 离线/隔离网络部署是真实用例；本地 Qwen 3/3.5 与 DeepSeek R1 的连接性对等很重要。8 个月后关闭。
#8276 ReMe reranker 接受空 api_key 4 链接 配置校验缺口导致晦涩的 "unexpected error"——用户希望快速失败并给出可操作的消息。
#7436 IM 中紧凑工具调用显示 3 链接 聊天通道噪音；企业 IM（飞书/钉钉）用户希望简洁渲染。
#5110 引用转后续追问（Perplexity 风格） 3 链接 基于选区的上下文注入是常见的 assistant UX 预期。

观察： 一个反复出现的主题是**"功能存在但不可读/不可发现"**——内存标签已生成但不可读（#8580）、默认 agent 可通过 API 编辑但在 UI 中被禁用（#8576）、插件设置路由丢失导航上下文（#8590）。这表明 UI/后端契约漂移值得专门审计。

5. 缺陷与稳定性

按严重程度排序，附修复 PR 状态：

严重 / 阻断

  1. #8592 — 创作者审核轮次永久无法裁定（链接）：REJECT 始终返回 422 "visual artifact reference references missing id"；同时捆绑了过期的 source_url 502 和忽略 CREATOR_FFMPEG_PATH 的 frame_stats。硬阻断——审核轮次永远无法关闭。尚无修复 PR。
  2. #8603 — 在自定义 OpenAI 兼容 provider 上 run_code 以空参数调用（链接）：在 kimi / kimi-codingplan 搭配 k3.1-pro 时，每次 run_code 调用都发出 {}；在校验时被拒绝。完全阻断该 provider 配置的工具使用。尚无修复 PR。
  3. #8580 — 内存标签索引从不重建（503）（链接）：标签已生成但不可读。尚无修复 PR。

高 4. #8585 — recall_history 在 Windows 上失效（链接）：\\?\ 扩展长度路径破坏了 SQLite 只读 URI。跨版本（2.2.x 起）。尚无修复 PR。 5. **#8517 — Hub Docker 以非 root 运行失败**（链接）：config.json 权限被拒绝。尚无修复 PR——加固环境的部署阻断。 6. #8538 — 多个工作区启用时 Matrix 插件失败（链接）：10 秒共享启动窗口仅覆盖第一个工作区。尚无修复 PR（相关 #8411 关闭了另一个 Matrix 问题）。

中 7. #8576 — 控制台中默认 agent 编辑被禁用（链接）：已有修复 PR：#8608。 8. #8595 — qwenpaw-creator v2.0.4 插件安装失败（"No package metadata"）（链接）：与 #8598 依赖检查重构（已关闭）相关。尚无确认的直接修复 PR。 9. #8590 — 插件设置路由丢失导航上下文（链接）：已关闭；无可见的关联修复 PR。

今日关闭（已解决）： #8549（配置校验，PR #8550）、#8365（Matrix 密钥，PR #8411）、#8533（cron 请求，PR #8535）、#8516（nginx 后 SSE X-Accel-Buffering）、#7857（ACP 关闭泄漏）、#8596（聊天重新打开）。

6. 功能请求与路线图信号

请求 链接 信号强度
用于紧凑 IM 工具显示的 tool_call_format 配置 #7436 强——已在打开的 PR #8610 中实现。可能进入下一个小版本。
用于后续上下文的引用/参考文本 #5110 强——已在打开的 PR #8609 中实现。
浏览器标签标题跟随会话名称 #8605 中等——小型、范围明确，面向多标签页重度用户。
创作者 UI 修复（按钮对比度、模型/密钥独立性） #8591 中等——创作者中的 UX 债务；按钮在白色背景上不可见。
Reranker 模型中心 #8472 强——大型功能 PR 审查中，可能进入 2.4.x。

对下一版本的预测： 紧凑工具调用显示（#8610）、引用转后续追问（#8609）和默认 agent 编辑（#8608）都是小型、自包含的 PR，已可落地——进入下一个控制台版本的概率很高。Reranker 模型中心（#8472）较大，可能推迟。

7. 用户反馈总结

痛点：

  • 版本错配困惑——多份报告混合了 UI 2.3.0b2、后端 2.4 和 reme_ai 0.4.2.0，使分流对用户和维护者都更加困难。
  • Windows 是二等公民——GBK 编码丢失（#8234）、\\?\ 路径破坏（#8585）、shell 取消挂起（#8604）。专门的 Windows CI 通道将带来回报。
  • 静默失败——接受空 api_key（#8276）、持久化无效配置（#8549）、丢弃字节的解码（#8234）。用户一致要求带清晰消息的快速失败校验。
  • UI/后端契约漂移——功能通过 API 可用但在 UI 中被禁用或损坏（#8576、#8590、#8580）。

积极信号： 用户正在贡献修复（多个 first-time-contributor PR：#8606、#8550、#8535、#373），长期停滞的 issue 正在关闭（#1453 在 8 个月后、#373 在 8 个月后）。满意度似乎中等偏好——挫败感集中在特定子系统（内存索引、Matrix、创作者），而非核心 agent 循环。

8. 待办关注

需要维护者关注的事项：

  • #373 — 动态 MCP 按会话工具持久化。自 2026-03-02 打开（约 8 个月），首次贡献者，今日刚关闭。值得确认合并并感谢贡献者。
  • #8234 — GBK/CP936 解码修复。自 2026-10-14 打开，XXL 规模，审查中。对中文 Windows 用户影响大；需要审查带宽。
  • #8236 — Ollama num_ctx 上下文大小。自 2026-10-14 打开，XL。本地模型用户是增长中的群体。
  • #8100 — 运行时解析媒体能力。自 2026-10-03 打开。支持图像的模型被静默拒绝——正确性缺陷，修复已就绪。
  • #8274 — 聊天切换时保留待处理的用户输入。自 2026-10-16 打开。与数据丢失相邻的 UX 缺陷。
  • #5110 — 引用转后续追问。自 2026-06-11 打开（约 5 个月）；现已有 PR（#8609），尽快闭环将是良好习惯。
  • #8592 — 创作者审核阻断。昨日提交，尚无维护者回应——最高优先级的新到项。

建议： 优先审查 #8234 和 #8100（均已就绪、高影响正确性修复），并为 #8592（创作者阻断）和 #8585（Windows recall_history 回归，跨版本）指派负责人。

ZeroClaw — zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw

ZeroClaw 项目摘要 — 2026-11-07

1. 今日概览

ZeroClaw 正处于高速安全加固阶段。活动非常活跃：过去 24 小时内更新了 25 个 issue 和 50 个 PR（13 个 issue 已关闭，13 个 PR 已合并/关闭，37 个 PR 仍处于开放状态）。主旋律是身份/访问控制与权限强制执行——多个 S0/S1 级发现（会话数据所有权绕过、SOP 通配符工具选择器、cron 审批绕过）正在被关闭，相应的修复 PR 正在审查中。一个依赖安全公告（vodozemac）阻断了 CI，并于当天完成修复。整体项目健康度在响应速度方面表现强劲，但大量 P1/风险：高 的安全项涌入 v0.9.0 里程碑，表明发布门禁 crunch 正在进行中。

2. 发布

过去 24 小时内无新版本发布。值得注意的是，多个已关闭的 issue 带有 release:v0.9.0 标签，表明针对 v0.9.0 的发布门禁工作正在积极推进。

3. 项目进展

今日关闭的 issue（共 13 个）包含有意义的安全与正确性修复：

  • #11127 [已关闭, P1, S0] 会话数据工具绕过了主体所有权检查（例如，sessions_history 可跨主体读取）。
  • #11123 [已关闭, P1, S0] SOP 执行接受了通配符工具选择器，而未要求 tools:execute。
  • #12051 [已关闭] sop_workshop apply 允许受限主体编写以操作员权限执行的共享 SOP。
  • #12046 [已关闭] 通配符工具选择器将不感知主体的工具（cron、schedule、对等消息传递、SOP 执行）泄露给非管理员主体。
  • #12272 [已关闭] vodozemac 0.11.0 RUSTSEC 公告破坏了安全质量门禁；已通过 PR #12273 修复（升级至 0.11.2）。
  • #12176 [已关闭] 延迟 MCP 工具列表以 HashMap 顺序排列，导致每个会话的 prompt 缓存失效。
  • #11962 [已关闭] 守护进程的 64 个活跃 RPC 会话在空闲时从未释放。
  • #12155、#12178、#12217、#12248、#12249 — 各类 bug/文档/任务关闭（快速入门消息传递、deliver_file 描述、邮件文档、不可运行工具的审批门禁、仪表盘配置页面可见性）。

推进主要工作流的关键开放 PR：

  • #9746 会话工具和 discord_search 的按代理所有权作用域（发布门禁，XL）。
  • #11149 在 RPC/工具/令牌撤销的写入点强制执行 cron 审批与权限。
  • #12239 通过会话效果保持当前权限（#11234 的后续）。
  • #12270 中继服务的 Web 仪表盘按节点主机（#10315 第二阶段）。
  • #9809 多模型提供商配置（长期运行，XL）。

4. 社区热点

按评论/反应最活跃：

  1. #10526（16 条评论）— RFC：仅追加的会话事件历史、确定性重放、派生代理流。审查后已关闭；标志着架构方向转向事件溯源运行时状态（补充 #9597 中的持久性工作）。
  2. #8132（13 条评论，1 👍）— 在 React/Vite 迁移之前评估 Rust/WASM UI。关于从构建/运行时中移除 Node.js 的长期架构辩论；目前需要作者行动。
  3. #10926（9 条评论）— Matrix send_via 将对等身份视为房间目标。
  4. #9779（7 条评论，P1）— 文档中记录的 sops_dir 默认值被守护进程静默忽略。

潜在需求： 社区正在推动 (a) 代理会话的运行时可观测性/可重放性，(b) 供应链简化（移除 Node.js），以及 (c) 配置默认值与守护进程启动路径之间一致、有文档记录的行为。

5. Bug 与稳定性

按严重程度排序（除非另有说明，均为今日报告/更新）：

严重程度 Issue 状态 / 修复 PR
S1 #12272 vodozemac RUSTSEC-2026-0445/-0451 在所有 PR 上破坏 CI 已关闭；修复 PR #12273 同日关闭
S1 #12263 严格提供商永久拒绝长工具密集型会话（422 tool_call_id），对话被砖化 开放；尚无修复 PR
S2 #12260 RPC cron/add/cron/patch 将请求视为操作员 shell 审批 开放；由 #11149 覆盖
S2/S0 #12279 通道启动竞态可能丢失在转录读取与上限之间追加的消息 开放；无修复 PR
S2 #9572 网关 WebSocket 轮次溢出 Tokio 工作线程栈（调试构建） 开放（P1，no-stale）
S2 #12052 速率限制器以客户端提供的首个 XFF 跳为键 → 回环豁免可被欺骗 开放；修复 PR #12114 审查中
S2 #10926 Matrix send_via 错误路由到对等身份 开放
P1 #9779 依赖文档中 sops_dir 默认值时 SOP 静默从不加载 开放

评估： 安全类 issue 正在快速关闭；功能性 S1（#12263 砖化会话）和启动数据丢失（#12279）是最高剩余风险，且尚无修复 PR。

6. 功能请求与路线图信号

  • #12181 Web 管理文档上传（#9488 的第一个第二阶段 Web 切片）— 可能近期实现；补充开放 PR #12269（Web 聊天语音控制）和 #11846（OpenRouter 余额设置）。
  • #9597 持久、可归属的对等代理轮次 — 符合 #10526 中接受的事件历史方向；v0.9.x 的强候选。
  • #8132 Rust/WASM Web UI — 战略性，非迫近；受阻于作者行动。
  • PR 驱动的在途功能：多模型提供商配置（#9809）、多插件注册表来源（#12216）、中继服务仪表盘（#12270）、Telegram 语音回复合成（#12276）。

预测： 下一个标记版本很可能是 v0.9.0 安全门禁裁剪（所有权作用域、cron 权限、SOP 授权）加上中继仪表盘和 Telegram/Discord 通道功能。

7. 用户反馈摘要

  • 以安全为核心的贡献者（Audacity88、IftekharUddin、JordanTheJet） 正在系统地审计主体/权限模型；发现被快速接受并关闭——这是健康分诊的标志，但也表明授权模型发布时存在缺口。
  • 运维痛点： 静默失败是反复出现的抱怨——SOP 不加载（#9779）、快速入门声称“未写入配置”却写入了（#12155）、长会话变得永久不可用（#12263）。用户重视可预测性胜过聪明。
  • 代理/部署用户 遇到现实世界的网关假设（#12052 中的 XFF 处理）；通道用户 报告启动时的消息丢失窗口（#12279）。
  • 满意度信号：依赖安全 issue 的快速同日关闭和主动跟进任务（#12248、#12261、#12280）表明维护者响应迅速；不满意度集中在静默错误配置和边缘情况会话损坏。

8. 积压关注

需要维护者关注的长期项目：

  • #8132（自 2026-06-22 开放，needs-author-action）— WASM UI 决策停滞；战略岔路口仍未解决。
  • #9572（自 2026-07-31，P1，no-stale）— 网关 WebSocket 轮次中的 Tokio 栈溢出；已接受但未修复。
  • #9779（自 2026-08-06，P1）— SOP 默认目录静默失败；用户影响高，无关联修复 PR。
  • #9746（自 2026-08-04，XL，发布门禁，needs-author-action）— 核心所有权作用域 PR；一个已搁置三个月的发布阻塞项。
  • #9809（自 2026-08-07，XL，needs-author-action）— 多模型提供商配置；大型、有价值且停滞。
  • #10926（自 2026-09-17，已接受，follow-up）— Matrix 路由 bug，无关联修复 PR。

数据来源：github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw，快照 2026-11-07。

本日报由 agents-radar 自动生成。

item.content:encoded:
OpenClaw Ecosystem Digest 2026-11-07

Issues: 377 | PRs: 500 | Projects covered: 5 | Generated: 2026-11-06 23:16 UTC

  • OpenClaw

OpenClaw Deep Dive

OpenClaw Project Digest — 2026-11-07

1. Today's Overview

OpenClaw remains in a high-velocity but stability-constrained phase: 377 issues and 500 PRs were updated in the last 24 hours, with 217 open/active issues and 361 open PRs versus 139 merged/closed PRs — a merge-to-open ratio that suggests review capacity is the bottleneck, not contributor supply. No new releases shipped, meaning the project is between release trains (current stable line is 2026.10.10, with 2026.11.5-beta.1 in prerelease). The dominant theme across today's activity is regressions and lifecycle/resource-management defects — gateway event-loop blocking, SQLite worker OOM, MCP child-process leaks, WAL checkpoint starvation, and prompt-cache invalidation — several of which are P0/P1 and marked as release blockers. Community engagement is workmanlike rather than euphoric: high comment counts on hard bugs (80 comments on one P0), near-zero reaction counts overall, and a large "stale" backlog of unresolved older reports.

7. User Feedback Summary

Pain points expressed by real users:

  • Upgrade reliability is the #1 frustration. Multiple reports describe upgrades that fail post-activation (#178291), block on migrations (#185656), or cannot even reach their own fix (#193962). Users on production installs are effectively pinned.
  • Resource leaks erode trust in long-running Gateways. Commenters quantify the damage themselves: ~144–145 MB per stdio MCP child (#164690), duplicated MCP spawns under claude-cli (#166017, #164690), cap-256 broker exhaustion (#166017). This is a sophisticated, production-operator audience.
  • Memory system behavior is confusing and lossy. Users report memory promote returning zero candidates in one workspace while siblings promote 50–90% (#164923), and nightly dreaming that never promotes (#150635) — the flagship "dreaming" feature is not delivering visible value to some users.
  • Silent failures and opaque errors recur as a theme: dropped Telegram callbacks (#126950), generic "changed while starting work" with no reason code across 16 call sites (#127195), unlabeled Code Mode internal errors (#167609), and revocations with no logged reason (#166964). Users are doing the diagnostic work the product should do.
  • Cost anxiety is tangible: users are hand-measuring cache-write tokens (#143017) and pleading for per-model usage logs (#13219).
  • Mobile/UI friction (tiny phone composer #139909, chat reload backtracking PR #193217, duplicate renders #123792) is a steady secondary stream.

Satisfaction signal: comment counts on hard bugs are high while reaction counts are near zero — users are engaged and diligent but not cheerleading. People clearly run OpenClaw in serious production configurations (Kubernetes, multi-agent orgs of 15 agents, Docker sandboxes), which is both a compliment to the project's capability and the source of its stability debt.

Cross-Ecosystem Comparison

Cross-Project Comparison Report — Personal AI Assistant / Agent Open-Source Ecosystem

Snapshot date: 2026-11-07 | Projects: OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, IronClaw, QwenPaw, ZeroClaw

1. Ecosystem Overview

The agent framework ecosystem is in a post-feature, pre-hardening phase: all four active projects have shipped their headline capabilities (multi-agent orchestration, memory/dreaming, plugins, channel gateways) and are now paying down the resulting stability debt. Activity is dominated by regressions and lifecycle bugs rather than new features, with security/authority models emerging as the new battleground (ZeroClaw) and operational reliability of long-running gateways as the universal pain point. The user base has matured into production operators running Kubernetes, multi-agent organizations, and hardened Docker deployments — their feedback is quantitative and diagnostic, not aspirational. Ecosystem health is bifurcated: contributor supply is strong everywhere, but maintainer review capacity is the binding constraint, evidenced by merge-to-open ratios well below 1.0 and months-old decision-blocked PRs. No project shipped a stable release in the window, suggesting the ecosystem is collectively between release trains.

3. OpenClaw's Position

Advantages vs peers:

  • Scale of community: 377 issues + 500 PRs updated in 24h is roughly 7–10× the activity of Hermes or QwenPaw and ~15× ZeroClaw. OpenClaw has the deepest contributor pool and the most sophisticated production operators (K8s deployments, 15-agent orgs, Docker sandboxes).
  • Broadest surface area: memory/dreaming system, MCP integration, plugin SDK, multi-channel (Telegram, msteams, iOS), cloud workers, Code Mode, and a Control UI — no peer matches this breadth.
  • Reference status: positioned as the "core reference" implementation; peers implicitly benchmark against it.

Technical approach differences:

  • OpenClaw runs a long-lived Gateway daemon as its architectural center — this is the source of both its power (persistent sessions, scheduled jobs, channel fan-in) and its stability debt (event-loop blocking, SQLite worker OOM, MCP child-process leaks). Peers like QwenPaw are more request/session-oriented with a lighter runtime footprint.
  • Heavier reliance on SQLite + worker processes and prompt caching for cost control — both currently pathological (cache invalidation #182891, worker OOM #191847), which is a cost and reliability exposure Hermes/ZeroClaw don't share at the same scale.
  • Mature plugin SDK + hosted catalog (with an open request #164620 to disable the catalog feed for air-gapped use) — a governance surface peers are still building.

Community size comparison: OpenClaw's comment activity on single hard bugs (80 comments on #160959) exceeds the entire daily engagement of QwenPaw or ZeroClaw. Hermes's top thread (#97681, 40 comments) is half of OpenClaw's hottest thread. OpenClaw is the ecosystem's gravitational center; the risk is that its review capacity is not scaling with its community.

  • Unknown: IronClaw (insufficient signal).

7. Trend Signals — Value for AI Agent Developers

Extracted from cross-project community feedback, ranked by strategic importance:

  1. Runtime reliability is the new feature. Every project's top bugs are daemon-level: event-loop blocking, SQLite worker OOM, child-process leaks, idle-session leaks, startup races. Developers should treat lifecycle resource management as a first-class design concern, not an afterthought. Expect framework-level solutions (supervisors, bounded workers, backpressure) to differentiate winners.

  2. Authority and approval governance is the next competitive surface. ZeroClaw's S0 ownership bypasses, Hermes's approval-gate bypass and Desktop approval requests, and OpenClaw's exec-approval gaps all point the same way: users want visible, enforceable, diff-based control over agent actions and memory/skill writes. Products that surface approval in the UI (not just CLI) and enforce at the write path will win trust.

  3. Session state is being re-architected as durable and replayable. OpenClaw (SQLite worker/WAL), Hermes (state.db + PostgreSQL seam #150332), ZeroClaw (event-sourced history #10526, durable peer turns #9597), and QwenPaw (chat-state cache) are all converging on event-sourced or append-only, cross-surface session stores. This is the single biggest architectural trend in the window.

  4. Cost visibility and cache correctness are monetizable pain. OpenClaw users hand-measure 21.3M cache-write tokens (#143017) and plead for per-model usage logs (#13219); ZeroClaw fixed a prompt-cache-order bug (#12176). Prompt-cache discipline and usage metering are now table-stakes for any framework used in production.

  5. Silent failures are the top trust-killer. Across all projects, the most-cited frustration is not crashes but silent drops, misreports, and no-reason errors (OpenClaw #127195, Hermes #148831/#130072, QwenPaw #8276/#8234, ZeroClaw #9779/#12155). Fail-fast validation with actionable reason codes is a cheap, high-impact differentiator.

  6. Upgrade paths are the weakest link. Update-path deadlocks (OpenClaw #193962), migration blocks (#185656), stale-snapshot restores (Hermes #147938), and version skew (QwenPaw 2.2/2.3/2.4). Reliable, reversible, self-verifying updaters are an underserved requirement — a viable investment area for tooling vendors.

  7. Multi-surface and cross-machine collaboration is the demand frontier. Hermes's #97681 (40 comments, needs-decision) and the Desktop/group-chat regression cluster; OpenClaw's multi-agent operator requests (#166678 hide-from-picker, #103067 subagent lifetime). Users are moving from single-agent to coordinated multi-agent, multi-surface deployments faster than the frameworks' session/authority models can support.

  8. Localization and offline/air-gapped operation are real markets. QwenPaw's offline-install (#1453), Windows/GBK issues (#8234, #8585), and OpenClaw's hosted-catalog-disable request (#164620) signal demand from regulated, air-gapped, and non-English production environments — an underserved segment.

Bottom line for developers: The ecosystem's center of gravity has shifted from what agents can do to whether they can be trusted to keep doing it — durably, safely, visibly, and affordably. Frameworks that solve session durability, authority enforcement, diagnosability, and update reliability will define the next release cycle; feature breadth is already commoditized.

Assessment: Stability burden is concentrated in Desktop/gateway session-state synchronization (multiple dokterdok reports) and Windows update/state integrity. Security-adjacent items (#150329, #141755) are worth triage given they touch the approval/guard boundary.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

High-likelihood candidates for upcoming versions:

  1. Cross-gateway bot collaboration — #97681 (needs-decision, most active): if approved, a multi-release architectural program (sessions, message delivery, gateway state flagged by sweepers).
  2. Ownership-scoped background skill writes — #142933 (skills.background_review_write_scope): restrict background self-improvement to curator-managed skills. Likely small-to-medium config feature.
  3. Desktop inline approval/edit modal — #84189: pairs naturally with #142933; high user demand.
  4. Email MCP integration package — #99030 (AgentMail/IMAP/SMTP): ecosystem push toward first-class email.
  5. Read-only Kanban/run/memory API endpoints — #149815: external integrations (Home Assistant "Hermes Voice") driving API surface requests.
  6. PWA installability for Webapp — #150345: trivial (manifest.json), high mobile payoff — likely quick win.
  7. llama.cpp slot save/restore — #141605 (local-model session continuity).
  8. Mobile voice bubbles + richer avatar — #148447.
  9. One user-visible agent name everywhere — #146434 (author wants to implement post-design).

Prediction: #150345 (PWA manifest) and #142933 (write-scope config) are the cheapest near-term wins; #84189 and #97681 are decision-gated and more likely to land in a following milestone.

7. User Feedback Summary

Pain points:

  • Data integrity & updates on Windows (#147938): stale-snapshot restore erodes trust in the updater — the most safety-critical complaint.
  • Approval workflows are invisible on Desktop (#84189, #142933): staged writes live only behind slash commands; users feel loss of control over agent self-modification.
  • Group-chat/Desktop sync is flaky (#143303, #143302, #143242, #143241, #143243, #147626): duplicate rooms, dropped messages, phantom "stopped" turns — friction for multi-surface users.
  • Security scanner over-blocking (#141755): legitimate community skills blocked, hurting ecosystem adoption.
  • Approval-gate bypasses (#150329): security-minded users flag holes in hardline/permission detection.
  • Context/scale limits (#108891 delegate 20k floor; #75130 unbounded proposal queue).

Positive use cases & adoption:

  • External integrations being built on Hermes — "Hermes Voice" Home Assistant bridge (#149815), mobile Android beta feedback (#148447), PWA request (#150345) — show growing surface-area use.
  • Vibrant plugin ecosystem: numerous catalog PRs (api-architect, BlazePhoenix, Construct, fal, CrashLab, Telos, lampstand, tiled-sessions, evalroute, lfg-alarm) indicate a healthy third-party developer community.

Satisfaction: Generally constructive; PR authors self-report AI-assisted, adversarially reviewed fixes (e.g., #148831) — a sign of engaged, technically sophisticated users. Dissatisfaction is mostly workflow friction and reliability, not fundamental capability gaps.

8. Backlog Watch

Long-unanswered or decision-blocked items needing maintainer attention:

  • #75130 (open since 2026-07-31, 7 comments) — Unbounded/dead skill-proposal queue under write_approval; a long-standing reliability debt.
  • #84189 (open since 2026-08-12, needs-decision, 4 👍) — Desktop approval modal; needs design decision.
  • #97681 (open since 2026-08-29, 40 comments, needs-decision) — Cross-gateway collaboration; highest-engagement item but gated on decision.
  • #86105 (open since 2026-08-14, needs-decision) — Force built-in memory enabled when external provider configured; small correctness fix awaiting decision.
  • #85342 (open since 2026-08-13, needs-decision, security/compat risk) — Docker refuse persistent reuse on config drift; safety-relevant, stalled.
  • #102928 — TTS prefetch fix; open and conflicting with main, blocking closure of #150010.
  • #150329 (new) — Approval-gate bypass via function/alias; security triage recommended promptly.
  • #147938 (P0, Windows data integrity) — Needs immediate maintainer ownership given data-loss potential.

Recommendation: Prioritize triage of the P0 Windows state.db issue (#147938) and the security bypass (#150329), unblock #102928, and clear the needs-decision backlog (#97681, #84189, #86105, #85342), which is the primary drag on both merged-PR throughput and community sentiment.

QwenPaw — agentscope-ai/QwenPaw

QwenPaw Project Digest — 2026-11-07

1. Today's Overview

QwenPaw shows high maintenance velocity: 22 issues and 38 PRs were touched in the last 24 hours, with a healthy 20 PRs merged/closed against 18 still open — a near 1:1 throughput-to-backlog ratio. Activity is dominated by stability and correctness fixes rather than new features: memory retrieval, provider config validation, channel plugins (Matrix), and Windows-specific path handling. No new release was cut, so the project sits on the 2.3.0b2 console line while 2.4 backend packages circulate in the field. Community engagement is modest per item (mostly 1–4 comments, zero reactions), indicating broad but shallow triage. Overall project health: strong — the maintainers are closing as fast as users file, and several long-standing issues (dating back to March 2026) were finally resolved.

2. Releases

None. No new releases in the last 24 hours. Note: the field is still split across 2.2.2, 2.3.0b2 (console), and 2.4 backend metadata, and several bug reports stem from this version skew (e.g., #8580 reports UI v2.3.0b2 with backend 2.4 and reme_ai 0.4.2.0).

3. Project Progress

The following closed/merged items represent concrete forward motion today:

Fixes landed (closed PRs / issues):

  • Provider config validation — #8550 (fixes #8549): out-of-range thinking_budget / max_input_length are now rejected on the write path instead of silently persisting and breaking provider discovery after restart.
  • Matrix channel recovery — #8411 (fixes #8365): cached sessions restored and missing E2EE device keys re-uploaded after server-side device drops.
  • Third-party agent scheduled tasks — #8535 (fixes #8533): Codex/Qoder cron tasks no longer fail with Third-party agent requests require text or attachments.
  • Dynamic MCP persistence — #373 (first-time contributor, open since March): dynamically loaded MCP tools now persist across session turns.
  • Console chat-switch state — #8600: /clear chats stay empty after reopening (fixes #8596).
  • Test stability — #8604, #7858: Windows shell cancellation hangs and unawaited-coroutine warnings resolved.

Still under review (high-value):

  • #8234 — GBK/CP936 decoding in read/edit/grep (fixes silent byte loss on Chinese Windows).
  • #8457 — automatic memory recall injected as reference context rather than synthetic assistant trajectory.
  • #8472 — reranker model center with multi-query precision history.

4. Community Hot Topics

Engagement is spread thin; the most-commented items (4 comments each) cluster around memory tagging and chat-state behavior.

Item Comments Link Underlying Need
#8580 Memory tag index returns 503 4 link Users enabling auto_memory_generate_tags expect tags to be readable, not just generated. Index rebuild reliability is a trust issue for the memory subsystem.
#8596 /clear message resurfaces 4 link Chat-state cache correctness — users rely on /clear semantics for privacy/reset workflows.
#1453 Offline install can't reach local Qwen 4 link Offline/air-gapped deployment is a real use case; local Qwen 3/3.5 connectivity parity with DeepSeek R1 matters. Closed after 8 months.
#8276 ReMe reranker accepts empty api_key 4 link Config validation gap causing cryptic "unexpected error" — users want fail-fast with actionable messages.
#7436 Compact tool call display in IM 3 link Chat-channel noisiness; enterprise IM (Feishu/DingTalk) users want terse rendering.
#5110 Quote-to-follow-up (Perplexity-style) 3 link Selection-based context injection is a common assistant UX expectation.

Observation: A recurring theme is "the feature exists but is unreadable/undiscoverable" — memory tags generated but unreadable (#8580), default agent editable via API but disabled in UI (#8576), plugin settings routes losing nav context (#8590). This suggests a UI/backend contract drift worth a dedicated audit.

5. Bugs & Stability

Ranked by severity, with fix-PR status:

Critical / Blocker

  1. #8592 — Creator review round permanently undecidable (link): REJECT always returns 422 "visual artifact reference references missing id"; also bundles expired source_url 502 and frame_stats ignoring CREATOR_FFMPEG_PATH. Hard blocker — a review round can never be closed. No fix PR yet.
  2. #8603 — run_code invoked with empty args on custom OpenAI-compatible providers (link): every run_code call emitted as {} on kimi / kimi-codingplan with k3.1-pro; rejected at validation. Blocks tool use entirely for that provider config. No fix PR yet.
  3. #8580 — Memory tag index never rebuilds (503) (link): tags generated but unreadable. No fix PR yet.

High 4. #8585 — recall_history broken on Windows (link): \\?\ extended-length path breaks SQLite read-only URI. Cross-version (2.2.x onward). No fix PR. 5. **#8517 — Hub Docker fails as non-root** (link): Permission denied on config.json. No fix PR — deployment blocker for hardened environments. 6. #8538 — Matrix plugin fails when multiple workspaces enable it (link): 10s shared startup window only covers the first workspace. No fix PR yet (related #8411 closed a different Matrix issue).

Medium 7. #8576 — Default agent edit disabled in console (link): Fix PR exists: #8608. 8. #8595 — Plugin install fails ("No package metadata") for qwenpaw-creator v2.0.4 (link): relates to #8598 dependency-check refactor (closed). No direct fix PR confirmed. 9. #8590 — Plugin settings route loses nav context (link): closed; no linked fix PR visible.

Closed today (resolved): #8549 (config validation, PR #8550), #8365 (Matrix keys, PR #8411), #8533 (cron requests, PR #8535), #8516 (SSE X-Accel-Buffering behind nginx), #7857 (ACP shutdown leak), #8596 (chat reopen).

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

Request Link Signal Strength
tool_call_format config for compact IM tool display #7436 Strong — already implemented in open PR #8610. Likely in next minor.
Quote/reference text for follow-up context #5110 Strong — implemented in open PR #8609.
Browser tab title follows session name #8605 Moderate — small, well-scoped, multi-tab power users.
Creator UI fixes (button contrast, model/key independence) #8591 Moderate — UX debt in Creator; button is invisible on white bg.
Reranker model center #8472 Strong — large feature PR under review, likely 2.4.x.

Prediction for next version: compact tool-call display (#8610), quote-to-follow-up (#8609), and default-agent editing (#8608) are all small, self-contained PRs ready to land — high probability for the next console release. Reranker model center (#8472) is larger and may slip.

7. User Feedback Summary

Pain points:

  • Version skew confusion — multiple reports mix UI 2.3.0b2, backend 2.4, and reme_ai 0.4.2.0, making triage harder for users and maintainers alike.
  • Windows is a second-class citizen — GBK encoding loss (#8234), \\?\ path breakage (#8585), shell cancellation hangs (#8604). A dedicated Windows CI lane would pay dividends.
  • Silent failures — empty api_key accepted (#8276), invalid config persisted (#8549), byte-dropping decode (#8234). Users consistently ask for fail-fast validation with clear messages.
  • UI/backend contract drift — features work via API but are disabled or broken in UI (#8576, #8590, #8580).

Positive signals: Users are contributing fixes (multiple first-time-contributor PRs: #8606, #8550, #8535, #373), and long-stale issues are being closed (#1453 after 8 months, #373 after 8 months). Satisfaction appears moderate-to-good — frustration is concentrated in specific subsystems (memory index, Matrix, Creator) rather than the core agent loop.

8. Backlog Watch

Items needing maintainer attention:

  • #373 — Dynamic MCP per-session tool persistence. Open since 2026-03-02 (~8 months), first-time contributor, just closed today. Worth confirming the merge and thanking the contributor.
  • #8234 — GBK/CP936 decoding fix. Open since 2026-10-14, XXL size, under review. High user impact on Chinese Windows; needs review bandwidth.
  • #8236 — Ollama num_ctx context sizing. Open since 2026-10-14, XL. Local-model users are a growing segment.
  • #8100 — Resolved media capabilities at runtime. Open since 2026-10-03. Image-capable models silently rejected — correctness bug with a ready fix.
  • #8274 — Preserve pending user input on chat switch. Open since 2026-10-16. Data-loss-adjacent UX bug.
  • #5110 — Quote-to-follow-up. Open since 2026-06-11 (~5 months); now has a PR (#8609), so closing the loop soon would be good hygiene.
  • #8592 — Creator review blocker. Filed yesterday, no maintainer response yet — highest-priority new arrival.

Recommendation: Prioritize review of #8234 and #8100 (both ready, high-impact correctness fixes), and assign an owner to #8592 (Creator blocker) and #8585 (Windows recall_history regression, cross-version).

ZeroClaw — zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw

ZeroClaw Project Digest — 2026-11-07

1. Today's Overview

ZeroClaw is in a high-velocity security-hardening phase. Activity is very high: 25 issues and 50 PRs updated in the last 24 hours (13 issues closed, 13 PRs merged/closed, 37 PRs still open). The dominant theme is identity/access control and authority enforcement — multiple S0/S1-class findings (session-data ownership bypass, SOP wildcard tool selectors, cron approval bypass) are being closed, with corresponding fix PRs in review. A dependency security advisory (vodozemac) blocked CI and was remediated same-day. Overall project health is strong on responsiveness, but the volume of P1/risk:high security items landing in the v0.9.0 milestone indicates a release-gate crunch is underway.

2. Releases

No new releases in the last 24h. Notably, several closed issues carry the release:v0.9.0 label, indicating active release-gate work toward v0.9.0.

3. Project Progress

Closed issues today (13 total) include meaningful security and correctness fixes:

  • #11127 [CLOSED, P1, S0] Session-data tools bypassed principal ownership checks (e.g., sessions_history readable cross-principal).
  • #11123 [CLOSED, P1, S0] SOP execution accepted wildcard tool selectors without tools:execute.
  • #12051 [CLOSED] sop_workshop apply allowed scoped principals to author shared SOPs executed with operator authority.
  • #12046 [CLOSED] Wildcard tool selectors leaked principal-unaware tools (cron, schedule, peer messaging, SOP execution) to non-admin principals.
  • #12272 [CLOSED] vodozemac 0.11.0 RUSTSEC advisories broke the Security quality gate; fixed via PR #12273 (bump to 0.11.2).
  • #12176 [CLOSED] Deferred MCP tool list in HashMap order busted prompt caching each session.
  • #11962 [CLOSED] Daemon's 64 live RPC sessions never released when idle.
  • #12155, #12178, #12217, #12248, #12249 — assorted bug/doc/task closures (quickstart messaging, deliver_file description, email docs, approval gate for non-runnable tools, dashboard config-page visibility).

Key open PRs advancing major workstreams:

  • #9746 Per-agent ownership scoping for session tools and discord_search (release-gate, XL).
  • #11149 Enforce cron approval and authority at the write across RPC/tools/token revocation.
  • #12239 Hold current authority through session effects (follow-up to #11234).
  • #12270 Relay-served web dashboard per-node host (#10315 phase 2).
  • #9809 Multi-model provider profiles (long-running, XL).

4. Community Hot Topics

Most active by comments/reactions:

  1. #10526 (16 comments) — RFC: append-only session event history, deterministic replay, derived agent streams. Closed after review; signals the architecture direction toward event-sourced runtime state (complements durability work in #9597).
  2. #8132 (13 comments, 1 👍) — Evaluate Rust/WASM UI before React/Vite migration. Long-running architectural debate about eliminating Node.js from build/runtime; currently needs-author-action.
  3. #10926 (9 comments) — Matrix send_via treats peer identities as room destinations.
  4. #9779 (7 comments, P1) — sops_dir documented default silently not honored by daemon.

Underlying needs: the community is pushing on (a) runtime observability/replayability for agent sessions, (b) supply-chain simplification (Node.js removal), and (c) consistent, documented behavior between config defaults and daemon startup paths.

5. Bugs & Stability

Ranked by severity (all reported/updated today unless noted):

Severity Issue Status / Fix PR
S1 #12272 vodozemac RUSTSEC-2026-0445/-0451 breaks CI on all PRs Closed; fix PR #12273 closed same day
S1 #12263 Strict provider permanently rejects long tool-heavy sessions (422 tool_call_id), conversation bricked Open; no fix PR yet
S2 #12260 RPC cron/add/cron/patch treat request as operator shell approval Open; covered by #11149
S2/S0 #12279 Channel startup race can lose a message appended between transcript read and cap Open; no fix PR
S2 #9572 Gateway WebSocket turns overflow Tokio worker stack (debug builds) Open (P1, no-stale)
S2 #12052 Rate limiter keys on client-supplied first XFF hop → loopback exemption spoofable Open; fix PR #12114 in review
S2 #10926 Matrix send_via misroutes to peer identities Open
P1 #9779 SOPs silently never load when relying on documented sops_dir default Open

Assessment: Security-class issues are closing fast; functional S1s (#12263 bricked sessions) and startup data-loss (#12279) are the highest residual risk without fix PRs.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

  • #12181 Web-managed document upload (first Phase 2 web slice of #9488) — likely near-term; complements open PR #12269 (web chat voice controls) and #11846 (OpenRouter balance settings).
  • #9597 Durable, attributable peer-agent turns — fits the event-history direction accepted in #10526; strong candidate for v0.9.x.
  • #8132 Rust/WASM web UI — strategic, not imminent; blocked on author action.
  • PR-driven features in flight: multi-model provider profiles (#9809), multiple plugin registry origins (#12216), relay-served dashboard (#12270), Telegram voice-reply synthesis (#12276).

Prediction: the next tagged release will most likely be the v0.9.0 security-gate cut (ownership scoping, cron authority, SOP authorization) plus relay dashboard and Telegram/Discord channel features.

7. User Feedback Summary

  • Security-focused contributors (Audacity88, IftekharUddin, JordanTheJet) are systematically auditing the principal/authority model; findings are being accepted and closed rapidly — a sign of healthy triage, but also of an authorization model that shipped with gaps.
  • Operational pain points: silent failures are a recurring complaint — SOPs not loading (#9779), quickstart claiming "No config written" while writing one (#12155), and a long session becoming permanently unusable (#12263). Users value predictability over cleverness.
  • Proxy/deployment users are hitting real-world gateway assumptions (XFF handling in #12052); channel users report message-loss windows at boot (#12279).
  • Satisfaction signals: fast same-day closures of dependency security issues and proactive follow-up tasks (#12248, #12261, #12280) suggest maintainers are responsive; dissatisfaction centers on silent misconfigurations and edge-case session corruption.

8. Backlog Watch

Long-lived items needing maintainer attention:

  • #8132 (open since 2026-06-22, needs-author-action) — WASM UI decision stalled; strategic fork in the road remains unresolved.
  • #9572 (since 2026-07-31, P1, no-stale) — Tokio stack overflow in gateway WebSocket turns; accepted but unfixed.
  • #9779 (since 2026-08-06, P1) — SOP default-dir silent failure; high user impact, no linked fix PR.
  • #9746 (since 2026-08-04, XL, release-gate, needs-author-action) — core ownership-scoping PR; a release blocker that has sat three months.
  • #9809 (since 2026-08-07, XL, needs-author-action) — multi-model provider profiles; large, valuable, and stalled.
  • #10926 (since 2026-09-17, accepted, follow-up) — Matrix routing bug with no fix PR attached.
